meta.description: Designs and analyzes stable-isotope-resolved metabolomics (SIRM / isotope tracing / fluxomics) experiments that measure metabolic ACTIVITY via 13C/15N/2H tracers, distinct from steady-state pool profiling. Covers tracer choice, isotopologue vs isotopomer, mass-isotopomer distributions (MID), fractional enrichment, the mandatory natural-abundance + tracer-purity correction (IsoCor, AccuCor), and the metabolic/isotopic steady-state vs non-stationary (INST-MFA) distinction.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 5 outputs use synthetic or independently-sourced real (accucor extdata) numeric inputs; no fabricated DOI/PMID, trial results, sample sizes, or p-values in any output.

practice_boundaries.detail: No diagnostic/prescriptive claims in any output; the Skill is scoped to bench-research metabolomics, not patient care; Input 4's cancer-cell-line question is answered as a tracer-design question only.

methodological_ground.detail: No principled methodological fallacy (no correlation-for-causation, no inverted conclusion via mismatched model) in any output. Input 3 exposed a real but lesser gap -- the SKILL.md steady-state snippet checks only the last time-point pair against a fixed threshold, which can pass a still-decelerating series as 'plateau'. This is an incompleteness/robustness gap, not a fallacy, so it does not meet the M3 FAIL bar; filed as a P1 recommendation instead.

code_usability.detail: All executed code (Inputs 1, 2, 3, 5) ran without syntax errors, missing dependencies, or infinite loops, using the real installed isocor 2.2.4 / accucor 0.3.1.9000 packages; Input 2's corrected output matched accucor's own shipped ground-truth reference to 2.8e-17.

functional_suitability.note: All documented use cases (isocor low-res correction, accucor high-res/QqQ correction, MID/enrichment math, steady-state check, tracer decision tree) covered and run-verified; docked 1 point for the steady-state check's incomplete robustness (see Input 3).

reliability.note: Common Errors table's causes are accurate and its length-mismatch entry matches the real isocor ValueError text exactly; docked 1 point because the real error text for the documented 'half-defined resolution' case is more generic than the table implies (verified, Inputs 3 & 5).

performance_context.note: SKILL.md ~187 lines, usage-guide kept separate, one reference example script; correct progressive disclosure, nothing loaded that isn't needed.

agent_usability.note: Consistent terminology and clear, runnable code patterns throughout; Feedback Design and Error Prevention both docked slightly for the same steady-state under-specification affecting Reliability.

human_usability.note: Description trigger language is strong and natural; Category-3 scene override applied to Forgiveness (strict input validation is correct design here) -- docked 1 point because isocor/accucor raise plain, non-Skill-specific ValueErrors rather than structured recovery codes.

security.note: No credentials, no destructive operations, no injection surface anywhere in SKILL.md, usage-guide, or the example script; pure numeric analysis on user-supplied arrays.

maintainability.note: Clean 3-file separation (SKILL.md / usage-guide.md / examples/isotope_correction.py), each with one clear responsibility; docked 1 point because only one worked example ships and no additional test fixtures are provided.

agent_specific.note: Description precisely disambiguates from 4 adjacent Skills (targeted-analysis, xcms-preprocessing, pathway-mapping, flux-balance-analysis), reducing mis-triggering; verified idempotent/deterministic; correctly hands flux-fitting off to INCA/13CFLUX2 rather than reimplementing MFA.

recommendations.title: Steady-state check only compares the last time-point pair
recommendations.problem: The documented steady-state snippet (`abs(fe[-1]-fe[-2]) < 0.02`) can return 'plateau reached' on a time course that is still clearly decelerating but not flat, licensing classical-MFA flux inference prematurely.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md's steady-state guidance checks only the final pair of points against a fixed threshold, with no check of the trend across the full time course.
recommendations.fix: Add guidance to require the delta to be shrinking (or below threshold) across at least the last 2-3 consecutive intervals, or recommend fitting a saturating-exponential curve to the full time course and checking its asymptote, per the already-cited Cheah & Young 2018 reference.

recommendations.title: Documented error text for 'half-defined resolution' is more specific than the real message
recommendations.problem: The Common Errors table implies IsoCor reports a resolution-specific problem when `mz_of_resolution`/`charge` are given without `resolution`; the real raised text is a generic 'unable to select a correction strategy' ValueError that does not name resolution at all.
recommendations.root_cause: The table paraphrases isocor's internal factory-selection failure rather than quoting the real (generic) message an agent will actually see.
recommendations.fix: Either quote the real isocor error text verbatim in the Common Errors table, or add a pre-check in the Skill's guidance that raises a more specific message before delegating to isocor's factory.

recommendations.title: AccuCor code pattern omits a real filesystem side effect
recommendations.problem: `natural_abundance_correction(path=...)` writes an output file next to the input path by default; the SKILL.md R snippet does not mention this side effect or the `output_base` parameter that controls it.
recommendations.root_cause: The snippet was written to show the return value, not the function's default file-write behavior.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line note to the AccuCor code block: 'writes <input>_corrected.xlsx next to the input by default -- pass output_base= to redirect it', so an agent following the pattern doesn't write into an unintended directory.

recommendations.title: No inline recovery guidance in the code snippets themselves
recommendations.problem: Both the isocor and accucor code blocks in SKILL.md show only the happy path; error handling exists only as prose in a separate Common Errors table, not as a try/except pattern in the snippets.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md separates 'how to call it' from 'what can go wrong' into different sections rather than integrating them.
recommendations.fix: Add one line to each code snippet (e.g. '# wrap in try/except ValueError -- see Common Errors table below') so the recovery path is visible at the point of use.
